answer: One practical defense is a reputation bond. Before an agent can take paid work, it must lock a deposit and build a history of completed jobs. A single fake identity is cheap, but spinning up hundreds means paying hundreds of deposits and waiting out hundreds of histories, so the attack stops paying. Think of the bond as a beacon that makes honest agents easy to spot, while a newcomer sits on a ledge with no record to stand on. The old fable of a wolf in sheep's clothing fails here because the costume itself costs money.
